display.title: Episode 395: The Strange Visitor (Chai Elul)
display.summary_short: A Chai Elul show: the birthdays of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, Shema with a five-year-old, the young Baal Shem Tov and a mysterious visitor in his forest cave, and a letter from a listener.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the day after Chai Elul 5749, as the program reached episode 395 after eight years on the air. Uncle Yossi explains that Chai Elul is the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov (born 1698) and the Alter Rebbe (born 1745), a day for learning their teachings and making good resolutions. Their main lesson is to serve Hashem with joy, as Dovid HaMelech writes, and especially in Elul, when Hashem shows everyone a smiling face. After the Hakochainik march, a five-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema. Story time tells of little Yisrolik, an orphan who studied Torah alone in a forest cave. When a stranger with a silvery beard asks if he is afraid, the boy repeats his father's last words: fear nothing and no one but Hashem. The stranger becomes his teacher, and the boy grows up to be the Baal Shem Tov. A splashdown into the mailbox brings a six-year-old listener's letter. The show closes with the special blessing of the coming Shabbos, the first night of Selichos and candle times.
display.lesson: Someone who fears only Hashem is never alone and need not be afraid of anything else; serve Hashem with joy.

date.note: Chai Elul (Monday 18 Sep) was announced 'last week' as upcoming; this Saturday night is the first Selichos, which fits Motzei Shabbos 23 Elul 5749. Tuesday show = 19 Sep 1989.
